Hyak KloneSystem Architecture
Hyak System Architecture
Hyak is part of the University of Washington's cyberinfrastructure plan to support world-class research in every department. Hyak is an ecosystem of high-performance compute (HPC) clusters and supporting infrastructure (e.g., data management, computational training, scientific consulting). Acknowledging our Pacific Northwest heritage, Hyak means "fast" in Chinook jargon. Counting 1, 2, and 3 translates to "ikt", "mox", and "klone" in this local trading language. The numbers are cluster names corresponding to the generation of Hyak cluster deployed. We are currently on the 3rd generation cluster for Hyak.

1. ikt
2. mox
3. klone
Klone cluster image
Component	Details
Cluster	klone
Service	January 2021 — Present
OS	Rocky 8
Compute	44,184 CPU cores [AMD Genoa, Intel Cascade Lake, Intel Ice Lake]
Accelerators	954 GPU cards [Turing, Ampere, Hopper]
Interconnect	100 Gbps [HDR100 Infiniband]
Topology	3:1 blocking 2-layer fat tree
Storage	2.7 PB GPFS
Namesake	Klone = 3 in Chinook jargon. Current active Hyak cluster.
